description: AeroFire is a team of four high school students from İskenderun, Hatay, Türkiye. Our region has lived through major wildfires, like the October 2020 Hatay fires. We are harmonizing NASA’s MODIS and VIIRS fire hotspot data and showing it on an interactive, automatically updated map, so both satellites tell one consistent story about the same fire. Our skills: Python, data science, AI, backend, frontend and design.
summary:
AeroFire is a web application that harmonizes NASA FIRMS active fire data from two satellite sensors, MODIS (about 1 km pixels) and VIIRS (375 m pixels), so that the same wildfire is not counted twice. The sensors see the same fires at different scales and use different confidence scales, which makes raw data misleading and breaks long-term records as MODIS nears the end of its life.

AeroFire fixes this with a three-step pipeline: standardized confidence values, matching of same-day detections within 1.5 km into one fire, and a shared daily 1 km grid. In our validated case (Belen, Hatay, 8-12 Oct 2020), the VIIRS/MODIS gap drops from 4.55x in raw data to 1.43x on the shared grid, and about one fifth of VIIRS detections, caused by a steel plant, are filtered out.

The live map covers all of Türkiye, is updated hourly, and shows the last 7 days up to 1 year. It includes a province report, a fire list with province and approximate district names, and a rule-based 5-level settlement risk prototype that uses wind (no AI or machine learning).
details:
WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS

NASA's MODIS (about 1 km pixels) and VIIRS (375 m pixels) sensors record the same wildfires at different scales, and their confidence values differ (MODIS 0-100, VIIRS low/nominal/high). Combining raw data double-counts fires and can create a false impression that wildfires increased after 2012. MODIS is nearing the end of its life, so this also threatens long-term records.

AeroFire downloads MODIS and VIIRS active fire data from NASA FIRMS and applies a three-step pipeline: (1) standardize the two confidence scales, (2) group detections of the same day that are within 1.5 km of each other into one fire, so the same fire is not counted twice, and (3) place detections on a uniform daily 1 km grid. Fixed thermal sources such as steel plants are filtered out. Raw and harmonized data can be compared side by side on an interactive map.

RESULTS

Validated case (Belen, Hatay, 8-12 October 2020): the raw VIIRS/MODIS ratio is 4.55x (191/42); on the shared 1 km grid it falls to 1.43x (50/35). 17 fires were formed, 3 seen by both sensors. About one fifth of VIIRS detections (50 of 241) came from a steel plant in Iskenderun and were removed.

Nationwide (last year, as of 15 Nov 2026): 51,007 detections, raw ratio 7.10x and 4.63x on the grid, 22,574 fire groups. This nationwide run has not been independently validated.

FEATURES

- Live map of all of Türkiye, updated hourly, with 7-day to 1-year views

- Province report (fire count, MODIS/VIIRS breakdown, peak FRP)

- Fire list with province and approximate district names

- A 5-level settlement risk prototype that uses wind direction, distance and fire power. It is rule-based; it uses no AI or machine learning, and its thresholds were chosen by the team.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Fire managers, emergency responders, scientists and land managers get one consistent picture of when and where burning occurred, instead of two incompatible records. This supports early warning, long-term trend analysis ("have wildfires really increased?") and keeps fire records comparable after MODIS ends. The project started from a real local disaster, the October 2020 Belen fire that spread to Iskenderun and Arsuz, where our team lives.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGY

Data: NASA FIRMS (MODIS, VIIRS S-NPP and NOAA-20). Other data: GADM 4.1 province boundaries, GeoNames villages and district centres, Open-Meteo wind. Backend: Bash, Awk, gnuplot and Python for data parsing, filtering, harmonization and spatial matching (including point-in-polygon), with JSON for data exchange. Frontend: HTML, CSS and JavaScript with Leaflet maps. Hosting and automation: GitHub Pages and GitHub Actions (hourly live update, daily archive update). No special hardware was used.

WHAT IS CREATIVE

We treat the problem as data inconsistency, not missing data: instead of choosing one sensor, we harmonize both and show the raw and harmonized views next to each other. A shared grid plus a same-day matching rule makes the sensors comparable with simple, explainable rules, and the whole system runs on free, open services.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Honest limits: VIIRS data was unavailable in August 2026 (Suomi NPP anomaly), and Suomi NPP delivery ended on 2 Nov 2026, so VIIRS now comes from NOAA-20 only. District names are matched to the nearest district centre, not real district boundaries. Population data is missing for many villages. The matching rule is a simple threshold validated on 5 days of Belen data. We documented these limits in the project instead of hiding them.

The repository includes slides and reports in the docs/ folder.
